mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the logical connective "or" (disjunction) is true?

options.A: P ∨ Q is true only when both P and Q are true.
options.B: P ∨ Q is false only when both P and Q are false.
options.C: P ∨ Q is true only when exactly one of P or Q is true.
options.D: P ∨ Q is always true regardless of the truth values of P and Q.

mcqs.answer: P ∨ Q is false only when both P and Q are false.
mcqs.explanation: For a disjunction P ∨ Q, the only case when it is false is when both components are false; in all other cases (true/false, false/true, true/true) it is true. Hence option B correctly describes the truth condition, while the other options misstate it.

mcqs.question: For the implication "If P then Q" (P \rightarrow Q), in which situation is the implication false?

options.A: P is true and Q is true
options.B: P is true and Q is false
options.C: P is false and Q is true
options.D: P is false and Q is false

mcqs.answer: P is true and Q is false
mcqs.explanation: An implication P \rightarrow Q is false only when the antecedent P is true while the consequent Q is false. In all other combinations (TT, FT, FF) the implication is true. Therefore option B correctly identifies the false case.

mcqs.question: The biconditional statement P \leftrightarrow Q is logically equivalent to which of the following expressions?
mcqs.explanation: A biconditional P \leftrightarrow Q is true exactly when P and Q have the same truth value—both true or both false. The expression (P \land Q) \lor (\lnot P \land \lnot Q) captures precisely those two cases, making it equivalent to the biconditional. The other options represent different logical relations.

mcqs.question: Consider the compound statement (P \lor Q) \rightarrow (P \land R). What is its truth value when P is false, Q is true, and R is false?

options.D: Cannot be determined from the given information

mcqs.explanation: First evaluate the antecedent: P \lor Q = false \lor true = true. Next evaluate the consequent: P \land R = false \land false = false. The implication true \rightarrow false is false. Hence the overall statement is false, making option B correct. The other options do not match the logical evaluation.
